# Independent Wire frames

`caller-frames.tsv` was produced by executing `read.ts`, `logout.ts` and
`wire-runtime.ts` from `dragginzgame/ic-auth-legacy` at
`e52a40be75dd9809d0528189d84b43fe96952ad9`, under `packages/client/src/generated/`.
Their SHA-256 values are retained in root `reference.sha256`. The root licence
applies to retained reference material. No replacement Rust encoder generated
these expected bytes.

The 18 named complete frames cover both unit requests, successful reads with
empty and 29-byte principals and zero/maximum deadlines, all five read refusals,
both deadline-bearing logout variants at zero/u64::MAX, invalid caller and all
four unavailable reasons. Empty principals are structurally valid transport;
these cases do not assert session-authority validity.

`admission-frames.tsv` adds 19 frames from the same revision's `credential.ts`
and `establish.ts`, with hashes in the same receipt. The explicit browser inputs
in `../admission-cases.mjs` cover both credential directions and proof variants,
both witness step tags, every nested field, empty claims/signature, absent and
maximum TTL, unnormalized scope text and every admission reply. Proof bytes and
time relationships are intentionally not cryptographically valid. Transport
acceptance is not verification. This corpus was generated by executing the old
browser codecs before running the new Rust encoder against it.

`../verify-reference.mjs` independently rechecks every frame in both directions
using the exact old generated browser codecs. It verifies source hashes, strips
TypeScript in a disposable directory and leaves the sibling checkout untouched.
Validated with Node 24.21.0 (including assertion prototype normalization):

```sh
node crates/ic-auth-wire/tests/verify-reference.mjs ../ic-auth-legacy
make qualify-wire-browser
```

The second command regenerates all four codecs from the new Rust schemas and
compares those too. Both runtimes must detach decoded bytes from mutable input
subarrays. The fixture tests accept redundant outer Postcard varints; signed-claims
canonicalization remains separate. SDK transport, actual browser lifecycle and
cryptographic verification remain outside this evidence. The script neither
patches nor vendors the reference runtime.
